Interactive Training Tutorial Santiago Rojas & Garrett Woodhouse Welcome Welcome to the tutorial to Build an Interactive Video Training. Use the menu on the left to navigate through the different steps. If you have any questions please contact me via email: santiago.rojasotero@usu.edu
1 Setup Programs 1.1 Install Unity 1.2 Install Meta Link 1.3 Verify the Installation

1 Setup Programs Before creating an interactive training, install and configure the required software: Unity Hub and Unity Editor Meta Link Complete each section below before continuing to the next chapter. 1.1 Install Unity Unity will be used to create and edit the interactive training project. 1.1.1 Step 1: Create a Unity account Create a free Unity account, or sign in if you already have one. 1.1.2 Step 2: Download Unity Hub Open the link below and download Unity Hub: Download Unity Personal 1.1.3 Step 3: Install Unity Open the Unity Hub installer. Follow the installation instructions. Sign in with your Unity account. Use Unity Hub to install the required version of the Unity Editor. Note: Unity Hub manages your Unity projects and installed Unity Editor versions. 1.2 Install Meta Link Meta Link allows your computer to connect to a compatible Meta Quest headset. 1.2.1 Step 1: Download Meta Link Open the installation page below: Download and install Meta Link 1.2.2 Step 2: Install the program Download the installer. Open the downloaded file. Follow the installation instructions. Sign in with your Meta account when prompted. Important: Do not connect the headset until the installation process asks you to do so. 1.3 Verify the Installation Before continuing, confirm that both programs work correctly. Unity Hub opens without displaying an error. You can sign in to your Unity account. At least one Unity Editor version is installed. The Meta Link application opens correctly. Your Meta Quest headset is recognized by the computer. After completing this checklist, continue to the next chapter.

3 Create a Scene This chapter explains how to create and configure a scene using the [Project Template Name] Unity project template. Since this may be your first time using Unity, each step includes a navigation path showing exactly where to navigate in Unity’s interface. Step 1: Import the Videos into Unity Begin by importing the videos that you plan to use in the training. 1.1 Locate the Videos Folder Locate the Project panel and navigate to the following folder: Assets > 1_SCENES > 2_PROJECT VIDEOS View screenshot Figure 3.1: Locate the Project Videos folder ✓ Expected result The 2_PROJECT VIDEOS folder is selected in the Project panel. 1.2 Import the Video Files Right-click the gray area on the right side of the Project panel and select Import New Asset. Select the video files from your computer. View screenshot Figure 3.2: Import video files into Unity ✓ Expected result Unity begins importing the selected video files. 1.3 Wait for the Import to Finish Wait for Unity to finish importing and processing the selected video files. ✓ Expected result All selected video files have been imported into Unity. 1.4 Rename the Videos Rename each video according to its position in the training sequence. Tip: Use short, descriptive filenames that reflect the order of the videos in your training. For example: 01_video_step_1 02_video_step_2 03_video_step_2.1 ✓ Expected result Each video has a unique and descriptive name that reflects its position in the training sequence. 1.5 Verify the Imported Videos Select the 2_PROJECT VIDEOS folder in the Project panel and verify that all the videos intended for the training are present. View screenshot Figure 3.3: Verify imported video files ✓ Expected result All videos intended for the training are visible in the Project panel. 1.6 Save Your Progress Navigate to the Unity menu bar and select: File > Save ✓ Expected result Changes to the current scene have been saved. Step 2: Create a New Scene Create a new scene for each video in the training. Important: In this project template, each scene corresponds to one video — so the number of scenes must match the number of videos you imported. For example, if you have three videos, the training will consist of three separate scenes. Locate the Project panel and open the following path: Assets > 1_SCENES > 1_1_PROJECT_SCENES Figure 3.4: Locate Scenes Path Check that you see the following pre-built scenes: 0_STARTING SCENE, 1_FIRST_SCENE, and LAST SCENE on the right side of the Project panel. Figure 3.5: Create Scenes To create your first scene you will use the 1_FIRST_SCENE as a template. Right-click in it and rename to your convenience. If you have more scenes, just copy and paste the same scene and rename accordingly TIP: Just like you did when you imported the videos, it is good practice to use a sequence number and a descriptive title to keep the scenes organized. For example: 01_scene_introduction 02_scene_demonstration 03_scene_practice To write the content of the training instructions (e.g., In this training you will be asked to complete …) locate the Hierarchy panel and open the path: SCENE START > TRAINING_INTRODUCTION Figure 3.6: Locate Path Locate the Inspector panel (at the right of the Hierarchy panel), and write the content of the instructions in the text box below the Header Text title. Figure 3.7: Write Training Instructions Save the progress. File > Save Step 3: Add a Video to the Scene Once you have renamed the scene, you are going to assign its corresponding video. Locate the scene you want to add the video to and double-click it to open it. Important: Double-clicking is required to open a scene — a single click is not enough. To confirm a scene is open, check that its name matches the name shown at the top of the Hierarchy panel. Figure 3.8: Check Scene Name In the Hierarchy panel, open the following path: SCENE START > MENU > VIDEO_PLAYER Figure 3.9: Locate Path Locate the Inspector panel, and in the Video Clip sub section click in the circle icon. Figure 3.10: Upload Videos Select the video clip you want to use from the window that appears. Figure 3.11: Select Video Confirm that the video appears by double-clicking on it Save the progress. File > Save Step 4: Set Up the Questions In this section, you will set up the following for the scene you just created: The instructions for each question The content of each question The content of the multiple-choice answers Which answer is correct The correct feedback (shown when the participant answers correctly) The corrective feedback (shown when the participant answers incorrectly) Locate the Project panel and open the path: Assets > 0_PREFABS Figure 3.12: Locate Path Drag one of the prefabs: question_four_multiple_answers or question_four_multiple_answers (depending on the type of question you want) into the gray area of the Hierarchy panel. Figure 3.13: Drag Question Click the question prefab, then locate the Inspector panel and the subsection EDIT EVERYTHING BELOW THIS. Figure 3.14: Edit Question Content Edit the question content. See the table below for more indications. FIELD WHAT TO DO INSTRUCTION TEXT Replace Write the content of the instructions here. QUESTION TEXT Replace Write the content of the question here. ANSWER CHOICES Write the content of each answer in its corresponding Answer Choice #field. CORRECT-ANSWER FEEDBACK Replace Write your correct feedback here. CORRECTIVE-ANSWER FEEDBACK Replace Write your corrective feedback here. To select the correct answer, enter its corresponding number in the Correct Answer Choice field In the image below, you will observe that the correct question for the answer How many people are around you in this room? is >5 that corresponds to the Answer Choice 2 which is already selected in the answer key Figure 3.15: Choose Correct Answer Repeat Steps 1–5 to add additional questions in the scene. Note: If you have to provide more detailed corrective feedback when the participant answers the same question incorrectly multiple times, you can enter additional feedback in the Corrective Feedback Text 2, Corrective Feedback Text 3, and Corrective Feedback Text 4 fields. The software will show the corrective feedback 2 upon the second time the client answers wrong, and so on. Save the progress. File > Save Step 4.1: Set up Question Order and Timing Locate Hierarchy panel and open the path SCENE START > MENU > SCENE MANAGER Figure 3.16: Locate Path Locate the Inspector panel and look for the Dynamic Sequence Setup section. Figure 3.17: Set up Question order and timing You will see two different panels. The Question Canvases and Pause At. The table bellow provides a description of each. LIST PURPOSE QUESTION CANVASES Determines the order in which the questions are presented. PAUSE AT Determines the time in the original video at which the question will be presented. Step 4.2: Configure Question Canvases Step 4.2.1 Configure the Questions Order Change the number right to Question Canvases to the number of questions that the scene will have. Drag the questions objects that you have from the Hierarchy panel to the Question Canvases. The order in which the question objects (e.g., question_four_multiple_answers) is displayed bellow the panel is the order in which the questions are shown in the video. Figure 3.18: Upload Questions in Scenes If you have more questions, drag them in their corresponding section. Step 4.2.2 Configure the Times in which the Questions will Appear Change the number right to Pause At to the number of questions that the scene will have. The number should be the same as the number you wrote in Question Canvases !. Write the time in the video where the questions should appear. Take into account that the numbers are in second, and they should correspond to the seconds in the Video. If you want the question to appear in the min 2:04 you should write 124. For example: Item Will Appear 0 60 seconds 1 120 seconds 2 180 seconds In this example, there different questions will appear at 1:00, 2:00, and 3:00 minutes. The first and last one are of four multiple answers and the second one is of two multiple answers. Figure 3.19: Three questions for Scene Step 4.3: Verify that the scenes are connected In the Project panel, go to Assets > 1_SCENES > 1_1_PROJECT_SCENES and double-click the video scene you want to configure. In the Hierarchy, expand SCENE START and select END_SCREEN. In the *Inspector, find End Screen Scene Controller > Scene Settings > Link To Next Scene**. In the Link To Next Scene field, enter the exact name of the scene that the Next Scene button should open. For the final video scene, enter LAST SCENE. Press Ctrl+S to save. Figure 3.20: Link Scenes Expected result: After the destination scene is enabled in the build profile, pressing Next Scene on the video’s end screen opens that scene. Step 5: Verify the Question Order Before continuing, confirm that: Every pause time has a corresponding question canvas. The pause times are arranged chronologically. The question canvases are arranged in the intended order. The number of items in both lists is identical. Each question is associated with the correct point in the video. Warning: Questions may appear at the wrong times when the order of the question canvases does not match the order of the pause times (Step 4.2) Step 6: Edit the Beginning Screen The beginning screen introduces the training before the video starts. In the Project panel, double-click on 0_STARTING SCENE Figure 3.21: Find Starting Scene Locate BeginSceneCanvas in the Hierarchy panel and expand Menu the canvas to locate Header Text. Figure 3.22: Locate Header Text In the Inspector panel, find the section TextMeshPro - Text (UI) (you might have to scroll down) ], and replace the existing text with the introduction for your training. You can double check the text in the Scene panel Figure 3.23: Change Training Title For example: Welcome to the caregiver training. In this module, you will observe a caregiver responding to a child during a daily routine. Tip: Keep the introduction brief, easy to read, relevant and consistent with the purpose of the training. Save the scene. Step 7: Check the End Screen Check the destination you set in Step 4.3 for each video scene. In the Project panel, double-click the video scene you want to check. In the Hierarchy, expand SCENE START and select END_SCREEN. In the Inspector, find End Screen Scene Controller > Scene Settings > Link To Next Scene. Enter the exact name of the next scene, without the .unity extension. For the final video scene, enter LAST SCENE. If you made a change, press Ctrl+S to save. Figure 3.24: Select END_SCREEN, find Scene Settings, and check Link To Next Scene ✓ Expected result Link To Next Scene displays the destination. The learner presses the end-screen button to open it. The button reads Continue in this example. Step 8: Add the Scene to the Build Profile Add each new video scene to the Scene List used by your active build profile. In the Project panel, double-click the new video scene to open it. Go to File > Build Profiles. Select the active platform or profile and click Open Scene List. Figure 3.25: Click Open Scene List in Build Profiles If the scene is missing from the list, click Add Open Scenes. Confirm that its checkbox is selected. Check that 0_STARTING SCENE, every video scene used in your training, and LAST SCENE are enabled. Figure 3.26: Use Add Open Scenes, then check that each required scene is enabled ✓ Expected result Every scene in the training flow has a checked box in the active Scene List. The example shows the three enabled template scenes. Test the connection: Close Build Profiles, open 0_STARTING SCENE, and enter Play mode. Follow the training and press the end-screen button after each video. Confirm that each button opens the intended scene and that the final video leads to LAST SCENE. Step 9: Save the Scene Save the scene after making any changes by pressing: Ctrl + S You should save the scene after: Assigning a video Changing question timestamps Adding question canvases Editing the beginning screen Editing the end screen Adding the scene to the build profile Step 10 - Scene Configuration Checklist Before moving to the next scene, confirm that: The scene has a clear and unique name. The correct video has been assigned. The video plays correctly. The number of pause times matches the number of questions. Each question canvas is in the correct position. The beginning-screen text has been updated. The next-scene name has been entered correctly. The scene has been added to the build profile. The scene has been saved. After completing this checklist, repeat the process for the next video in the training.
